nodes.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of instances, to an instance $(n, es, K)$ of MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE that is well formed and feasible (its graph has a spanning tree with at least $K$ leaves). Bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.
nodes.title: The decision problem MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, es, K)$ of MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE is feasible when there are a sublist $T$ of $es$ (a list obtained from $es$ by deleting entries) with no repeated entries and exactly $n - 1$ entries, and a set $L$ of at least $K$ vertices in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, such that the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ is an entry of…
nodes.title: Feasible MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE instances

nodes.summary: An instance of MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE is a triple $(n, es, K)$ of a natural number $n$ (the number of vertices), a list $es$ of pairs of natural numbers (the edge list) and a natural number $K$ (the bound on the number of leaves).
nodes.title: Instances of MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE

nodes.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, es, K)$ of MAXIMUM LEAF SPANNING TREE is well formed when $n > 0$, the list $es$ has no repeated entries, and every entry $(u, v)$ of $es$ satisfies $u < n$, $v < n$ and $u \ne v$, and $(v, u)$ is not an entry of $es$.
